what_it_proves: Costco's value-access model operates at mass consumer scale.
boundary: Net sales do not prove membership quality by themselves.

what_it_proves: The warehouse model kept growing in the annual period.
boundary: Growth can come from price, traffic, new units, mix, or fuel; it needs decomposition before stronger consumer claims.

what_it_proves: Merchandise sales plus membership fees create a very large consumer-facing revenue base.
boundary: Total revenue does not show product-level margin or household affordability by category.

what_it_proves: Customers pay for access before buying the next basket, making membership a direct economic layer.
boundary: Membership fees do not prove unlimited pricing power or that every member is equally engaged.

what_it_proves: Costco's model converted very large revenue into profit in the annual period.
boundary: Net income is company-level profit, not basket-level cash proof or category-level return.

what_it_proves: The value-access engine remained active in a current quarterly period.
boundary: Quarterly sales do not isolate traffic from price, new warehouses, gasoline, or currency.

what_it_proves: Current sales growth supports Costco as a live value-retail example, not only a historical one.
boundary: High growth still needs margin, renewal, and traffic support before a durability claim.

what_it_proves: Existing-store/channel momentum was visible, not only new-unit expansion.
boundary: Comparable sales can be affected by inflation, fuel, currency, and mix.

what_it_proves: Adjusted comps give a cleaner read that member shopping behavior was still healthy.
boundary: Adjusted comps still do not prove renewal quality or category-level unit volume.

what_it_proves: Digital convenience is attaching to the membership/warehouse model instead of replacing it.
boundary: Digital growth can cannibalize warehouse economics or carry lower margin if fulfillment cost is high.

what_it_proves: The customer pays upfront because the retailer has earned trust that the next basket will be good value.
boundary: Trust can break if value gap narrows, renewal slows, or promotional pressure rises.

value: membership fee plus high-volume merchandise throughput
what_it_proves: Costco gets paid twice: direct access fees and merchandise economics supported by traffic and volume.
boundary: The model still depends on physical execution, inventory discipline, supplier terms, and consumer value perception.
